title: Global functions on a proper reduced scheme over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-scheme-over-base] whose structure morphism is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The set $C$ of connected components (maximal nonempty connected subsets) of $X$ [def-weil-connected-scheme] is finite, its members are open and closed, and the map of $k$-algebras $\prod_{c\in C}k\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ that sends $(a_c)$ to the section with constant value $a_c$ on the open subscheme $c$ is an isomorphism. If $X$ is empty, $C$ is empty and both rings are the zero ring, with the product interpreted as the empty product.

source.place: Tag 0BUG, label lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections, clauses (1)-(3), specialized to an algebraically closed field

proof.text: Properness gives locally finite type and quasi-compactness over Spec k. Apply LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace to obtain IsNoetherian X. The proved NoetherianSpace.finite_connectedComponents and NoetherianSpace.locallyConnectedSpace give finitely many clopen connected components.

Choose a representative p(c) of each component c and let U(c) be its connected component, an open subset. Membership x in U(c) is equivalent to ConnectedComponents.mk x = c. Each U(c) is nonempty and connected. Its inclusion is an open immersion with closed image, hence a closed immersion; composing with the proper structure map shows U(c) is proper over k. It is reduced as an open subscheme of X. Apply the existing general-scheme declaration GlobalSectionsBijective.of_isAlgClosed (recorded by lem-sc-global-functions, whose prose specializes it to curves). The scalar map k -> Gamma(U(c),O) is bijective. Compose with Opens.topIso to obtain E(c):k ≃+* Gamma(X,U(c)). Functoriality identifies E(c) with restriction of the actual scalar map of X.

Define R:Gamma(X,O) -> product_c Gamma(X,U(c)) by restriction. If R(s)=R(t), restrict at the component containing x and apply its germ map to get equal germs at every x; sheaf section_ext gives s=t. For surjectivity, glue an arbitrary family on U(c). On an overlap, a point would give mk x=c=d, so for c unequal to d the intersection is empty and compatibility follows by section_ext. For c=d it is reflexivity. The opens cover X, so existsUnique_gluing gives a global section with the required restrictions.

Compose the coordinatewise equivalences E(c) with the inverse of R to obtain e:(C -> k) ≃+* Gamma(X,O). Its restriction to U(c) is E(c)(a(c)). For constant a this equals restriction of the actual scalar section; injectivity of R proves scalar compatibility. Taking germs on the component c=mk x and using germ_res_apply proves the specified germ formula. If X is empty then C is empty by surjectivity of mk; the function ring is subsingleton, and the sheaf empty-cover instance makes Gamma(X,O) subsingleton. The gluing construction also applies to this empty cover.
